text:
emma: heads up - trying to run the one-liner installer on a corp Win10 box (PowerShell 5.1) and it fails with a TLS/handshake error. installer is `iwr https://install.redwood.ai | iex`. error: "The underlying connection was closed: Could not establish trust relationship for the SSL/TLS secure channel."

ryan: corporate proxies often intercept TLS. do you get the same error if you `iwr https://install.redwood.ai -UseBasicParsing`?

emma: i tried `iwr` alone and it downloaded HTML (proxy login). i can't run `iex` on corp image due to execution policy (AllSigned). tried bypassing with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` but still the handshake fails.

theo: two separate problems: 1) proxy/proxied cert causing TLS failures, 2) execution policy preventing script execution. Workaround: download the installer on a machine with working network, verify SHA256, then copy the script to the corp machine and run with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\\install.ps1` after verifying source.

emma: tried that but when running installer it created ~/.redwood/config.yaml under the user profile, but our environment sets REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH to point at `C:\redwood\global_config.yaml` and the installer then merges incorrectly, producing duplicate profiles. local serve then complains about malformed config.

ryan: ah yes there was a merge bug if both REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH and a user-level config existed; installer did a naive concatenation and left stray `-` markers. this was filed as DX-560.

emma: minimal repro I used: 
```
$env:REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH = 'C:\redwood\global_config.yaml'
# run installer which writes user config
# then cat both and see duplicated `profiles:` keys
```

theo: workaround: move the global config aside, run installer to create a clean user config, then use `redwoodctl profiles import --from C:\redwood\global_config.yaml --set-current` to import safely. that CLI command respects overrides and will fail if it detects duplicate keys.

emma: import worked, but small UX note: `--set-current` expects the profile name, not a boolean. confused at first. maybe docs should be clearer.

ryan: good catch. i'll add an argument alias `--auto-select` in the next PR to make it accept `true`/`false` values and pick the first profile when importing. ticket DX-561.

docs-bot: created docs PR draft devex/cli/install.md with guidance for corp proxies, manual download verification, and config import tips.

emma: last thing - after import, `redwoodctl local serve` attempts to bind to 0.0.0.0 and fails on corp due to firewall. Is there a flag to restrict host?

theo: yeah `redwoodctl local serve --host 127.0.0.1` works. also you can set `local.host: 127.0.0.1` in config to make it persistent. we should add a note in the quickstart.

emma: thanks. overall flow: manual download -> copy -> run with bypass -> import global config using CLI -> set host to 127.0.0.1 -> local serve works. will paste steps into the ticket. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for redwoodctl v0.12.3 9: includes config import safety and installer docs (PR #2198). ETA 42m.

ryan: follow-up: folks on older PowerShell should consider using the cross-platform curl + sh installer on WSL or Git Bash: `curl -fsSL https://install.redwood.ai | sh` if your environment permits.
